report.summary: During the requested investigation window, payment-service p95 latency rose 4.0x, from 0.24s to 0.94s. Logs also report timeouts calling fraud-api and unavailable fraud checks, supporting investigation of this dependency as a contributor. The evidence does not establish fraud-api's internal failure mechanism or prove it was the initial cause.

likely_causes.title: Slow or unavailable responses from fraud-api contributed to payment-service latency degradation
likely_causes.rationale: payment-service logs explicitly report timeouts calling fraud-api after 2000ms and fraud checks being unavailable, consistent with an upstream dependency contributing to payment-service latency. These observations do not establish the dependency's internal failure mechanism or temporal precedence.

supporting_evidence.detail: 20 sampled WARN occurrences report “upstream timeout calling fraud-api after 2000ms” (version=v1.4.2; sample timestamps 2026-10-26T12:29:34+00:00 to 2026-10-26T13:07:34+00:00).
11 ERROR occurrences report “PaymentAuthorizationException: fraud check unavailable” (version=v1.4.2; sample timestamps 2026-10-26T12:06:34+00:00 to 2026-10-26T13:03:34+00:00).
Threshold-validated payment-service p95 latency rose 4.0x, from 0.24s to 0.94s; anomaly_detected=True.

next_steps: Check fraud-api latency, availability, and errors during the investigation window; the query returned zero matching fraud-api timeout documents, which is not evidence of healthy service.
Correlate payment-service traces and timeout occurrences with request latency to estimate the dependency's contribution.
Measure payment-service request rate and resource saturation; the supplied findings do not establish increased traffic or contention.
Review deployment and version history before attributing the issue to a regression; the supplied findings do not establish a deployment cause.
